---
title: "Troubleshooting & FAQ"
description: "The failure modes people actually hit, in the order they usually hit them."
---

## The game won't launch {#the-game-wont-launch}

**Symptom:** with EOS Reimagined dropped in, the game exits instantly, a dialog like *"The
procedure entry point EOS_… could not be located"* appears, or a Unity/Mono game throws
`EntryPointNotFoundException`. With Epic's original library it starts fine.

**Cause:** the game is resolving an EOS symbol the library doesn't export — which means you are
running an **old build**. Since the full-surface milestone *(2026-07-14)*, EOS Reimagined
exports **every** function the SDK headers declare (638 of them); the ones without real behavior
answer an honest `EOS_NotImplemented` instead of not existing. A current artifact simply cannot
die this way.

**What to do:** rebuild from current source (or grab a fresh CI artifact) and drop the new
library in. If it still happens, run the
[import census](tracing.qmd#inspect_gamepy-will-this-game-even-load) against the game and your
exact library — it names every missing symbol and its severity:

```sh
python3 tools/inspect_game.py "/path/to/Game/" --our-library build/libEOSSDK-Linux-Shipping.so
```

Anything **LOADER-FATAL** in that report against a current build is a bug — open an issue with
the census output.

## The game runs, but a feature does nothing

That's the flip side of the full export surface: a family that isn't really built yet — voice,
achievements, cloud saves, commerce, anti-cheat, and friends (the full list is on the
[roadmap](roadmap.qmd#present-but-not-functional)) — *loads and answers honestly* instead of
crashing. Queries complete with `EOS_NotImplemented`, getters report empty, and nothing
pretends to have worked. The game keeps running; that feature is simply absent.

If you want to see exactly which stubbed calls a game leans on, run it with
[`EOSR_TRACE=lifecycle`](tracing.qmd) — every stub answer lands in the trace — and attach that
to an issue. Real-game data is what prioritizes which family gets built next.

## Peers don't see each other {#peers-dont-see-each-other}

Work down the list; each item catches real cases:

1. **Same subnet or configured seeds?** Discovery defaults to UDP broadcast. Different subnets,
   guest Wi‑Fi isolation, and most VPN interfaces will not carry it. Put both machines on the same
   Wi‑Fi/switch, or configure every participant's IPv4 address in `peer_seeds` on every machine.
2. **Firewall?** Allow **UDP 55789–55798** (in and out, including broadcast) and inbound **TCP
   from the LAN** for the game — see [Networking & firewalls](networking.qmd). On Windows, if
   you ever clicked "Cancel" on the firewall prompt, the block rule persists: check
   *Windows Defender Firewall → Allowed apps*.
3. **Same game, same build, both patched?** Every player must run the *same title* with EOS
   Reimagined dropped in. The handshake binds the game's product/sandbox/deployment IDs and the
   wire version — a different game, a different game *version* with different IDs, or a player
   still on Epic's DLL simply cannot complete a handshake.
4. **Same discovery range?** If anyone overrode [`discovery_ports`](configuration.qmd), everyone
   must use the identical range. Peer seeds use this range too; there is no separate seed port.
5. **`enable_lan` still true?** `enable_lan: false` (or `EOSR_ENABLE_LAN=0`) runs the platform
   with no peer network at all — deliberately invisible.
6. **Port range full?** Ten instances per machine per range; the eleventh finds no free
   discovery port and comes up peerless.

Still stuck? `EOSR_TRACE=lifecycle` on both machines and compare: machine A should show
`discover` for B, then `handshake`, then `adopt`. Where the sequence stops is what's broken —
no `discover` means broadcasts/seeds aren't arriving (network/firewall/config); `discover` without `adopt`
means the TCP dial-back or handshake is failing (firewall on the *other* box, or mismatched
game/version).

## Both instances act like one player

**Symptom:** two copies on one machine (or two machines) fight over one identity, or a game
shows one confused player.

**Cause:** they're sharing a profile key. On one machine that shouldn't happen (instances take
exclusive [profile slots](identity-and-profiles.qmd)) — but copying a whole data directory to
another machine, or pointing two instances at the same `EOSR_DATA_DIR`, ships `profile.key`
along, and one key is one player. The mesh will refuse the second connection under an
already-connected identity.

**Fix:** give each player their own data directory (`EOSR_DATA_DIR=~/eosr/p1`, `…/p2`), or
delete the copied `profile.key` on the second machine so it mints its own.

## I moved machines and became a new player

Your identity is the `profile.key` file, and it stayed behind. Copy it from the old machine's
data directory into the new one — that file *is* your identity. (And back it up: nobody can
reissue it.) See [Identity & profiles](identity-and-profiles.qmd).

## Voice chat doesn't work

Correct, for now: the RTC families are honest stubs — the game loads, room calls answer
`EOS_NotImplemented`, and no audio is carried. (Even the reference emulator's RTC merely managed
rooms without carrying voice.) Track it on the [roadmap](roadmap.qmd). Meanwhile: Discord
exists, and a LAN party is usually one room anyway.

## Achievements / cloud saves / DLC checks are missing

Same story — Achievements, Stats, Leaderboards, PlayerDataStorage, TitleStorage, and Ecom are
[stubs](roadmap.qmd#present-but-not-functional): the game loads and runs, the queries complete
honestly with `EOS_NotImplemented`, and the features stay absent until each family is really
built. The `unlock_dlcs` config key is accepted today but honestly reported as ignored until
Ecom actually answers ownership checks.

## The overlay never appears / invites do nothing

There is no overlay, on purpose — this is a headless library, and it reports the overlay as never
visible rather than pretending. Games whose *only* join path is an overlay click (Presence/
Session/Lobby "join accepted" notifications) can register those notifications, but nothing fires
them yet. The designed answer is the [external social companion](../developers/internals/companion-client.qmd):
a separate local app that shows your authenticated LAN peers and tells the SDK inside the game to
fire the normal join callback. It's a planned milestone, not shipped.

## Frequently asked

**Can I play with a friend who's on real Epic/EOS?**
No, and we don't intend to make that work. EOS Reimagined speaks its own reconstructed protocol
between copies of *itself* and never contacts Epic's servers. It is emulator-to-emulator, and
letting unauthenticated copies onto Epic's live services is explicitly a non-goal — see
[Scope & non-goals](scope.qmd).

**Does this work over the Internet?**
EOS Reimagined does not perform Internet discovery, NAT traversal, or relaying. It can bootstrap over
an existing routed private network by configuring every participant's IPv4 address in `peer_seeds`;
Tailscale or another VPN is then responsible for reachability. That is VPN-assisted play, not native
Internet matchmaking.

**Is this a crack? Will it bypass anti-cheat?**
No and no. It does not remove ownership checks a game does elsewhere, it implements none of
Epic Anti-Cheat, and anti-cheat bypass is out of scope permanently. A game that hard-requires
EAC to reach multiplayer is not going to get there with this library. The project's position on
piracy and cheating is [stated in full here](scope.qmd).

**Windows says the DLL is untrusted / SmartScreen complains.**
You replaced a signed Epic DLL with an unsigned open-source one; that's expected. Build it
yourself from source if trust is the concern — that's rather the point of FOSS.

**Where does it keep my files?**
Everything lives in one per-user data directory — profile keys, `eosr.json`, traces:
`~/.local/share/eos-reimagined` on Linux, `%LOCALAPPDATA%\eos-reimagined` on Windows,
overridable with `EOSR_DATA_DIR`. Nothing is written into the game folder except the library you
copied there yourself, or the manager-owned `eosr-bootstrap.json` beside it when a managed instance
is active. That descriptor contains only the selected data-directory path; profile material remains
outside the game.

**How do I report a bug well?**
The easy way: run the game through
[`alpha_runner.py`](tracing.qmd#alpha_runnerpy-one-safe-diagnostic-game-run) and attach the
`*-bundle` directory it produces — it already merges the census, run metadata, and trace, with
display names, arguments, and absolute paths stripped. The manual way: reproduce with
`EOSR_TRACE=lifecycle` and attach the run's `trace.jsonl` (it contains labels and fingerprints,
not real IDs or payloads — glance at `runtime.json` before sharing, since it echoes your display
name), plus the game, OS, and — if the game won't load — the `inspect_game.py` output. Then
[open an issue](https://github.com/anishgoyal1108/EOS-Reimagined/issues/new).
